text: Architect web interfaces synthesizing mid-century Swiss Typographic design, industrial manufacturing manuals, and retro-futuristic aerospace/military terminal interfaces.
Construct digital environments that project raw functionality, mechanical precision, and high data density while discarding conventional consumer UI patterns.
Pick ONE visual archetype per project and commit to it.
Do not alternate or mix both visual modes within the same interface.
Use high-contrast light modes with newsprint or off-white substrates for Swiss Industrial Print.
Rely on monolithic, heavy sans-serif typography for Swiss Industrial Print.
Outline structural grids with visible dividing lines for Swiss Industrial Print.
Use aggressive, asymmetric negative space with oversized, viewport-bleeding numerals or letterforms for Swiss Industrial Print.
Use primary red as alert or accent color for Swiss Industrial Print.
Use dark mode exclusively for Tactical Telemetry.
Present high-density tabular data for Tactical Telemetry.
Use monospaced typography absolutely for Tactical Telemetry.
Integrate technical framing devices such as ASCII brackets and crosshairs for Tactical Telemetry.
Apply simulated hardware limitations such as phosphor glow, scanlines, and low bit-depth rendering for Tactical Telemetry.
Make typography the primary structural and decorative infrastructure.
Treat imagery as secondary to typography.
Use extreme variance in scale, weight, and spacing in typography.
Classify macro-typography as Neo-Grotesque or Heavy Sans-Serif.
Use optimal web fonts Neue Haas Grotesk Black, Inter Extra Bold Black, Archivo Black, Roboto Flex Heavy, Monument Extended for macro-typography.
Deploy macro-typography at massive scales using fluid typography such as clamp(4rem, 10vw, 15rem).
Apply extremely tight, often negative tracking from -0.03em to -0.06em to macro-typography.
Apply highly compressed leading from 0.85 to 0.95 to macro-typography.
Use exclusively uppercase casing for structural macro-typography.
Classify micro-typography as Monospace or Technical Sans.
Use optimal web fonts JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Space Mono, VT323, Courier Prime for micro-typography.
Set micro-typography scale fixed and small from 10px to 14px or 0.7rem to 0.875rem.
Apply generous tracking from 0.05em to 0.1em to micro-typography.
Apply standard to tight leading from 1.2 to 1.4 to micro-typography.
Use exclusively uppercase casing for micro-typography metadata, navigation, unit IDs, and coordinates.
Classify textural contrast typography as High-Contrast Serif.
Use optimal web fonts Playfair Display, EB Garamond, Times New Roman for textural contrast.
Use textural contrast typography exceedingly sparingly.
Subject textural contrast typography to heavy post-processing such as halftone filters or 1-bit dithering.
Prohibit gradients, soft drop shadows, and modern translucency in the color system.
Colors simulate physical media or primitive emissive displays.
Choose ONE substrate palette per project and use it consistently.
Never mix light and dark substrates within the same interface.
Use background #F4F4F0 or #EAE8E3 for Swiss Industrial Print light mode.
Use foreground #050505 to #111111 for Swiss Industrial Print light mode.
Use accent #E61919 or #FF2A2A as the ONLY accent color for Swiss Industrial Print light mode, restricted to strike-throughs, thick structural dividing lines, or vital data highlights.
Use background #0A0A0A or #121212 for Tactical Telemetry dark mode.
Avoid pure #000000 as background for Tactical Telemetry dark mode.
Use foreground #EAEAEA as primary text color for Tactical Telemetry dark mode.
Use accent #E61919 or #FF2A2A with the same rules for Tactical Telemetry dark mode.
Use Terminal Green #4AF626 optionally for a single specific UI element only, never as general text color.
Omit Terminal Green if it doesn't serve a clear purpose.
Adhere strictly to CSS Grid architectures for layout.
Anchor elements precisely to grid tracks and intersections rather than floating.
Use solid borders 1px or 2px solid extensively to delineate distinct zones of information.
Use horizontal rules spanning the entire container width frequently to segregate operational units.
Create layouts oscillating between extreme data density and vast calculated negative space framing macro-typography.
Reject border-radius absolutely; all corners must be exactly 90 degrees.
Replace standard web UI conventions with utilitarian, industrial graphic elements.
Utilize ASCII characters to frame data points.
Use ASCII framing such as [ DELIVERY SYSTEMS ], < RE-IND >.
Use ASCII directional characters such as >>> and ///.
Integrate registration, copyright, and trademark symbols as structural geometric elements rather than legal text.
Integrate crosshairs at grid intersections.
Integrate repeating vertical lines barcodes, thick horizontal warning stripes, and randomized string data to simulate active mechanical processes.
Engineer simulated analog degradation into the frontend via CSS and SVG filters.
Transform continuous-tone images or large serif typography into dot-matrix patterns via halftone and 1-bit dithering.
Achieve halftone dithering via pre-processing or CSS mix-blend-mode multiply overlays combined with SVG radial dot patterns.
Apply repeating-linear-gradient to terminal interface backgrounds to simulate CRT scanlines.
Apply a global, low-opacity SVG static or noise filter to the DOM root to introduce physical grain across both dark and light modes.
Utilize display: grid; gap: 1px; with contrasting parent/child background colors to generate razor-thin dividing lines without complex border declarations.
Construct the DOM using precise semantic tags such as <data>, <samp>, <kbd>, <output>, <dl>.
Implement CSS clamp() functions exclusively for macro-typography.
The layout must appear mathematically engineered.
It rejects conventional web padding in favor of visible compartmentalization.
